import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1036

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1036](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1036)
- [AlHa91] Alon, N. and Hajnal, A., *Ramsey graphs contain many distinct induced subgraphs*.
  Graphs Combin. (1991), 1-6.
- [ErHa89b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On the number of distinct induced subgraphs of a graph*.
  Discrete Math. (1989), 145-154.
- [Sh98] Shelah, Saharon, *Erdős and Rényi conjecture*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1998), 179-185.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos1036

/--
`G` contains at least `k` many induced subgraphs which are not pairwise isomorphic, that is,
there is a family of at least `k` many sets of vertices whose induced subgraphs are pairwise
non-isomorphic.
-/
def HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝒮 : Set (Set V), (𝒮.Pairwise fun s t => IsEmpty (G.induce s ≃g G.induce t)) ∧
    k ≤ (𝒮.ncard : ℝ)

/--
`G` contains no complete bipartite graph, and no complement of a complete bipartite graph, on
more than `m` vertices as an induced subgraph.
-/
def NoLargeInducedBipartite {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : Set V) (a b : ℕ),
    (Nonempty (G.induce s ≃g completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) ∨
      Nonempty (G.induce s ≃g (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b))ᶜ)) →
    (s.ncard : ℝ) ≤ m

/--
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices which does not contain a trivial (empty or complete) graph on
more than $c\log n$ vertices. Must $G$ contain at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many induced subgraphs
which are not pairwise isomorphic?

This is true, and was proved by Shelah [Sh98].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1036.lean"]
theorem erdos_1036 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
Alon and Hajnal [AlHa91] proved that $G$ must contain at least
$$\exp\left(n(\log n)^{-O(\log\log n)}\right)$$
many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1036.variants.alon_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G
          (Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ (-(C * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89b] proved that if $G$ does not contain a complete bipartite graph or its
complement on more than $c\log n$ vertices then $G$ contains at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many
non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1036.variants.erdos_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      NoLargeInducedBipartite G (c * Real.log (n : ℝ)) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1036

findings.description: The hypothesis `NoLargeInducedBipartite G ...` excludes induced complete bipartite graphs and their graph complements. This imposes conditions inside both parts—independence for a biclique, completeness for its complement—that the cited Erdős–Hajnal result does not impose. Its hypothesis forbids balanced complete or empty cross-pairs, with arbitrary edges inside the parts. These properties differ even after allowing constant rescaling: joining two Ramsey graphs produces a linear-sized complete cross-pair while all induced bicliques/co-bicliques remain logarithmic in size. As a finite check, the join of two 5-cycles has no induced biclique/co-biclique on more than 4 vertices, but its halves form a complete 5-by-5 cross-pair; all 59,049 ordered disjoint vertex-set pairs were checked exhaustively.
findings.source_evidence: [ErHa89b], §2, Theorem 2, p.154, assumes that K_{c log n,c log n} occurs in neither G nor its complement. Its notation (2), p.146, defines G[A,B] = (A ∪ B, E ∩ [A,B]), retaining only cross-edges (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-24.pdf). [Sh98], Introduction, explicitly defines Bipartite(G) as the maximum k for which there are disjoint k-element sets A₁,A₂ with all cross-edges present or all absent, without restrictions inside either set (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9707226, 627.tex).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace this premise with a balanced homogeneous-pair condition. For example, define `NoLargeHomogeneousPairs G m` by `∀ A B : Finset V, Disjoint A B → A.card = B.card → ((∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, G.Adj x y) ∨ (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, ¬ G.Adj x y)) → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ m`, and use it at `m = c * Real.log (n : ℝ)`. Bounding total size instead is equivalent after rescaling c by 2. Leave the induced-subgraph counting conclusion unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The source counts isomorphism classes of induced subgraphs; Lean instead asks for a sufficiently large family of vertex sets whose induced graphs are pairwise non-isomorphic.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite V, every such family injects into the quotient of Set V by induced-graph isomorphism. Conversely, choosing one representative of each quotient class yields a pairwise non-isomorphic family of exactly the quotient's cardinality. Thus the definition is equivalent to k being at most the number of isomorphism classes. This equivalence was proved for every finite V and real k in `Review1036.many_iff_isoCount`.

reformulations.difference: Relative to Shelah's explicit formulation, Lean uses natural logarithms and non-strict homogeneous-set bounds, with an eventual quantifier rather than an explicit size threshold.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Because the claim quantifies over every positive c, changing logarithm base simply rescales c by the positive constant log 2. Strict bounds imply weak bounds; conversely, for n ≥ 2, a weak bound c log n implies a strict bound 2c log n, so applying the strict formulation at 2c recovers the weak one. These transformations preserve constants uniform in n and G. On ℕ, `∀ᶠ n in atTop, P n` is exactly `∃ n₀, ∀ n ≥ n₀, P n`. The logarithm/strictness equivalence and the eventual-threshold equivalence were proved in the scratch file.

`G` has no disjoint vertex sets of equal cardinality greater than `m` such that all cross-edges
are present or all cross-edges are absent. Edges within either set are unrestricted.
-/
def NoLargeHomogeneousPairs {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B : Finset V, Disjoint A B → A.card = B.card →
    ((∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, G.Adj x y) ∨ (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, ¬ G.Adj x y)) →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ m

/--
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices which does not contain a trivial (empty or complete) graph on
more than $c\log n$ vertices. Must $G$ contain at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many induced subgraphs
which are not pairwise isomorphic?

This is true, and was proved by Shelah [Sh98].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1036.lean"]
theorem erdos_1036 : answer(True) ↔

      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
Alon and Hajnal [AlHa91] proved that $G$ must contain at least
$$\exp\left(n(\log n)^{-O(\log\log n)}\right)$$
many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1036.variants.alon_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G
          (Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ (-(C * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89b] proved that if neither $G$ nor its complement contains a balanced
complete bipartite graph with more than $c\log n$ vertices in each part as a (not necessarily
induced) subgraph, then $G$ contains at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many non-isomorphic induced
subgraphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1036.variants.erdos_hajnal :

      NoLargeHomogeneousPairs G (c * Real.log (n : ℝ)) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1036
